t: Portuguese establish permanent settlement in Macau
c: After a few decades, hostilities between the Portuguese and Chinese ceased and in 1557 the Chinese allowed the Portuguese to occupy Macau.

t: Afonso de Albuquerque seizes Persian Gulf ports
c: To enforce a trade monopoly, Muscat and Hormuz in the Persian Gulf were seized by Afonso de Albuquerque in 1507 and in 1515, respectively.

t: Albuquerque expedition cruises Red Sea near Aden
c: In 1513, while trying to conquer Aden, an expedition led by Albuquerque cruised the Red Sea inside the Bab al-Mandab and sheltered at Kamaran island.

t: António Correia conquers Bahrain for Portugal
c: In 1521, a force under António Correia conquered Bahrain, ushering in a period of almost 80 years of Portuguese rule of the Gulf archipelago.

t: Portuguese fleet reaches Suez in Red Sea
c: In the Red Sea, Massawa was the most northerly point frequented by the Portuguese until 1541, when a fleet under Estevão da Gama penetrated as far as Suez.

t: Portuguese navigators gather in Seville to serve Charles I
c: By 1516, several Portuguese navigators conflicting with King Manuel I of Portugal gathered in Seville to serve the newly crowned Charles I of Spain.

t: Juan Sebastián Elcano reaches Spice Islands
c: Juan Sebastián Elcano completed the voyage, reaching the Spice Islands in 1521.

t: Treaty of Zaragoza divides Spice Islands and Philippines

t: King Ferdinand urges Juan Ponce de León to explore new lands
c: In 1512, to reward Juan Ponce de León for exploring Puerto Rico in 1508, King Ferdinand urged him to seek these new lands.

t: Diego Velázquez commissions expedition to Yucatán Peninsula
c: In 1517, Cuba's governor Diego Velázquez de Cuéllar commissioned a fleet under the command of Hernández de Córdoba to explore the Yucatán Peninsula.

t: Hernán Cortés receives command of Mexican expedition

t: Pascual de Andagoya explores western South America
c: A first attempt to explore western South America was undertaken in 1522 by Pascual de Andagoya.

t: Pizarro forms partnership to explore south
c: In 1524, he formed a partnership with priest Hernando de Luque and soldier Diego de Almagro to explore the south, agreeing to divide the profits.

t: Pizarro travels to Spain to secure royal support
c: In the spring of 1528, Pizarro sailed for Spain, where he had an interview with king Charles I.

t: Urdaneta sails from Cebu across Pacific Ocean
c: Urdaneta set sail from San Miguel on the island of Cebu on 1 June 1565, but was obliged to sail as far as 38 degrees North latitude to obtain favorable winds.

t: Urdaneta's expedition reaches Acapulco
c: The ship reached the port of Acapulco, on 8 October 1565, having traveled 12,000 miles (19,000 kilometres) in 130 days.

t: Dutch rebellion against Spanish rule begins
c: In 1568, the Dutch rebelled against the rule of Philip II of Spain leading to the Eighty Years' War.

t: Philip II becomes King of Portugal
c: In 1580, Philip II became King of Portugal, as heir to its Crown.

t: Cornelis de Houtman gathers information on Spice Islands
c: In 1592, Cornelis de Houtman gathered information on the Spice Islands in Lisbon.

t: Francis Drake sails North American coast during circumnavigation
c: The English privateer Francis Drake sailed along the coast in 1579 north of Cabrillo's landing site while circumnavigating the world.

t: Juan Fernández claims discovery of Southern Continent
c: Juan Fernández, sailing from Chile in 1576, claimed he had discovered the Southern Continent.

t: Jacob Le Maire and Willem Schouten round Cape Horn
c: In 1615, Jacob Le Maire and Willem Schouten's rounding of Cape Horn proved that Tierra del Fuego was a relatively small island.

t: Pyotr Beketov appointed Yenisei voevoda in Siberia
c: In 1627, Pyotr Beketov was appointed Yenisei voevoda in Siberia.

t: Beketov founds Yakutsk on Lena River
c: Beketov was sent to the Lena River in 1631, where in 1632 he founded Yakutsk and sent his Cossacks to explore the Aldan River and farther down the Lena, to…

t: Maksim Perfilyev founds Bratsk ostrog
c: Maksim Perfilyev, who earlier had been one of the founders of Yeniseysk, founded Bratsk ostrog on the Angara in 1631.

t: Kurbat Ivanov discovers Lake Baikal
c: In 1643, Kurbat Ivanov led a group of Cossacks from Yakutsk to the south of the Baikal Mountains and discovered Lake Baikal, visiting its Olkhon Island.

t: Ivan Moskvitin reaches Pacific Ocean

t: Kurbat Ivanov draws first Russian map of Far East
c: Based on Moskvitin's account, Kurbat Ivanov drew the first Russian map of the Far East in 1642.

t: Vassili Poyarkov reaches upper Zeya River
c: In 1643, Vassili Poyarkov crossed the Stanovoy Range and reached the upper Zeya River in the country of the Daurs, who were paying tribute to the Manchus.

t: Mikhail Stadukhin discovers Kolyma River
c: In 1644, Mikhail Stadukhin discovered the Kolyma River and founded Srednekolymsk.

t: Dezhnyov reaches Anadyr River mouth
c: A small group led by Dezhnyov reached the mouth of the Anadyr River and sailed up it in 1649, having built new boats from the wreckage.

t: Dutch East India Company established
c: Soon the Dutch East India Company established trade with the East, having imported 6 million porcelain items from China to Europe between 1602 and 1682.

t: Decameron first translated into German
c: Giovanni Boccaccio’s Decameron was first translated into German by the physician, Henry Stainhowel, who died in 1482.

t: Cranach moves to Wittenberg and paints Reformers
c: Cranach lived in Wittenberg after 1504 and painted portraits of Martin Luther, Philip Melanchthon and other leaders of the German Reformation.

t: Conrad Celtes appointed professor at Ingolstadt
c: Ingolstadt for a time had Reuchlin as professor and, in 1492, Conrad Celtes was appointed professor of poetry and eloquence.

t: Death of Alexander Hegius
c: Among the noted schoolmasters was Alexander Hegius, who taught at Deventer for nearly a quarter of a century, till his death in 1498.

t: Vesalius publishes De humani corporis fabrica
c: Following after is Andreas Vesalius's publication of De humani corporis fabrica (On the Fabric of the Human body) in 1543.

t: Andreas Vesalius born in Brussels
c: Andreas Vesalius was born in 1514 around midnight in Brussels, then part of Habsburg Netherlands, to a long lineage of doctors.

t: Charles VIII invades Italy to capture Naples
c: In 1494, Charles VIII led a large army into Italy to capture Naples, which had been seized by Alfonso V of Aragon.

t: Henry II continues French royal building projects
c: Following the death of Francis I in 1547, his successor King Henry II continued to enlarge and embellish the château.

t: Philibert Delorme constructs Château d'Anet
c: The Château d'Anet was constructed by Philibert Delorme for Diane de Poitiers, the favorite mistress of Henry II, between 1547 and 1552.

t: Pierre Assézat begins construction of hôtel d'Assézat
c: Pierre Assézat, a wealthy woad merchant, launched the first phase of construction in 1555–1556.

t: Hôtel d'Assézat construction resumes under Dominique Bachelier
c: After Bachelier's death in 1556 the construction work stopped; it was restarted in 1560 under the direction of Dominique Bachelier, son of Nicolas.

t: Church of Saint-Eustache construction begins in Paris
c: The Church of Saint-Eustache, in the center of Paris, was begun by François I and is second in size only to Notre-Dame among Paris churches.

t: Catherine commissions Jean Bullant to build gallery above bridge
c: After his death in 1570, Catherine asked Jean Bullant to build a picturesque gallery (1576) atop the bridge.

t: Ottoman conquest of Hungary ends Hungarian Renaissance
c: The Ottoman conquest of Hungary in 1526 put an abrupt end to the short-lived Hungarian Renaissance.

t: Aristotele Fioravanti rebuilds Cathedral of the Dormition
c: In 1475 the Bolognese architect Aristotele Fioravanti came to rebuild the Cathedral of the Dormition in the Moscow Kremlin, damaged in an earthquake.

t: Ivan III commissions Terem Palace in Kremlin
c: In 1485, Ivan III commissioned the building of a royal Terem Palace within the Kremlin, with Aloisio da Milano being the architect of the first three floors.

t: Italian architect Aleviz Novyi arrives in Moscow
c: In 1505, an Italian known in Russia as Aleviz Novyi or Aleviz Fryazin arrived in Moscow.

t: Cornelis Floris de Vriendt completes Antwerp city hall
c: An architect directly influenced by the Italian masters was Cornelis Floris de Vriendt, who designed the city hall of Antwerp, finished in 1564.

t: Printing press established in Utrecht

t: Low Countries have printing shops in 21 cities
c: By 1481 the Low Countries had printing shops in 21 cities and towns.

t: New Islamic coinage system introduced
c: Between 696 and 699, the caliph introduced a new system of coinage of gold, silver, and bronze.

t: Marwan ibn al-Hakam founds Marwanid Umayyad line

t: Abd al-Malik restores Umayyad control over Caliphate
c: His eldest son and successor Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan restored Umayyad control over the Caliphate after defeating the Zubayrids in 692.

t: Abbasids overthrow Marwan II and Umayyads
c: In 750, the Abbasids overthrew Caliph Marwan II, and most of the Umayyad family were slain.

t: Caliph Uthman killed in rebellion
c: Mounting resentment against Uthman's rule in Iraq and Egypt and among the Ansar and Quraysh of Medina culminated in the killing of the caliph in 656.

t: Ansar and Quraysh expel Umayyads from Medina
c: The Ansar and Quraysh of Medina also took up the anti-Umayyad cause and in 683 expelled the Umayyads from the city.

t: Marwan expels Zubayrid governor from Egypt

t: Abd al-Malik signs peace treaty with Byzantium

t: Byzantine solidus replaced with Islamic dinar
c: In 693, the Byzantine gold solidus was replaced in Syria and Egypt with the dinar.

t: Abd al-Malik completes Dome of the Rock
c: In 691/692, Abd al-Malik completed the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem.

t: Umayyads defeat Byzantines at Sebastopolis
c: The war with the Byzantines had resumed under his father after the civil war, with the Umayyads defeating the Byzantines at the Battle of Sebastopolis in 692.

t: Tariq ibn Ziyad invades Visigothic Kingdom
c: Musa's Berber mawla, Tariq ibn Ziyad, invaded the Visigothic Kingdom in 711 and within five years most of Hispania was conquered.

t: Deaths of al-Hajjaj and Qutayba
c: The deaths of al-Hajjaj in 714 and Qutayba in 715 left the Arab armies in Transoxiana in disarray.

t: Tang defeat Arabs at Battle of Aksu
c: The Tang Chinese defeated the Arabs at the Battle of Aksu in 717, forcing their withdrawal to Tashkent.

t: Yazid II reimpose jizya, sparking revolts

t: Major Berber Revolt breaks out
c: In 739, a major Berber Revolt broke out in North Africa, which was probably the largest military setback in the reign of Caliph Hisham.

t: Marwan II ends Khazar war with invasion

t: Khorasani Arab discontent after Battle losses
c: Discontent among the Khorasani Arabs rose sharply after the losses suffered in the Battle of the Defile in 731.

t: Yazid III proclaimed caliph, kills al-Walid II
c: In 744, Yazid III, a son of al-Walid I, was proclaimed as caliph in Damascus, while his army killed al-Walid II.
